metadata.title: GPU Purchase Review & AI System Setup | SonarWave Technologies
metadata.description: Review your GPU server or workstation purchase before you commit. SonarWave checks requirements and vendor quotes, then helps configure, test and hand over your on-premises AI system.

pains.title: Avoid an expensive purchase that does not do the job.
pains.description: AI software changes quickly. Your hardware has to support the work you actually need to do.

items.pain: “Is this GPU quote right for us?”
items.impact: Too much hardware wastes budget. Too little—or the wrong configuration—limits what you can run.
items.solution: We check the quote against your models, expected users and facility requirements.
items.outcome: A written recommendation you can take to leadership.

items.impact: A cloud service may not fit your data requirements. A local system still needs the right capacity and access controls.
items.solution: We specify an on-premises system and review how data, models and external services will be handled.
items.outcome: A buying and setup plan built around your data requirements.

items.impact: GPU hardware can sit idle while your team works through software, access and deployment problems.
items.solution: We configure the AI software, test agreed workloads, and document the setup for your team.
items.outcome: A tested system and a practical handover.

delivery.eyebrow: FROM PURCHASE TO A WORKING SYSTEM
delivery.title: We help make the decision.
delivery.titleSecondLine: Then help put it to work.
delivery.description: Procurement and hands-on AI setup in one engagement path. You can start before a purchase or with hardware you already own.

stages.title: Review & specify
stages.description: Define the workloads. Check GPU memory, software compatibility, facility needs and vendor quotes.

stages.title: Source & configure
stages.description: Support sourcing, then set up the operating system, networking, secure access, inference software and models.

stages.title: Test & hand over
stages.description: Test agreed workloads and user demand. Document the setup and walk your team through operating it.

delivery.accountability: Agree what success looks like before delivery: the workloads to run, the users to support and the checks the system must pass.

items.question: Can we start with just a quote review?
items.answer: Yes. The purchase review is a separate engagement. You receive the recommendation and decide whether you want help with sourcing, setup or handover.

items.question: We already own GPUs. Can you help?
items.answer: Yes. We can review your existing hardware and planned workloads, identify setup or compatibility gaps, and scope configuration and testing.

items.question: Why involve SonarWave alongside our IT team or vendor?
items.answer: Your team knows the business; your vendor knows its products. We connect your workload requirements to the proposed hardware and the AI software it needs to run, then help with setup and testing.

items.question: How are pricing and hardware sourcing handled?
items.answer: We agree the service scope, fee and schedule before work starts. Hardware, licences and cloud usage are separate. If sourcing is included, the proposal sets out the purchasing responsibilities and costs.

items.question: Does on-premises AI keep all our data local?
items.answer: That depends on the full setup. External APIs, telemetry, model downloads and access controls need to be reviewed. We plan the deployment around your data requirements; running a model locally does not by itself guarantee privacy or compliance.

sample.title: What a GPU Purchase Review covers.
sample.description: This is an example of the review format, not a client report or a hardware recommendation. Your review is based on your workloads, quotes and agreed scope.
sample.scenario: Example brief: a team wants a local AI assistant for internal documents and is comparing GPU server quotes.

sections.title: 1. Requirements
sections.description: Record the models, user demand, response-time needs, data restrictions and budget. Identify missing information before choosing hardware.

sections.title: 2. Quote assessment
sections.description: Compare each quote with the requirements. Note GPU memory, software support, storage, networking, warranty and any assumptions the vendor needs to confirm.

sections.title: 3. Installation readiness
sections.description: Check power, cooling, rack or workstation space, network access and who owns installation and system access.

sections.title: 4. Recommendation & validation
sections.description: Explain the recommended direction, unresolved risks and checks to complete before ordering. Define what the system must demonstrate during acceptance testing.

sample.closing: The outcome is a decision record: what to buy, why it fits, and what still needs to be checked.
